title: Opportunistic Scheduling and Eviction Contracts — Design & Runbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This page describes the opportunistic scheduling model and the formal eviction contracts used by the runtime to preserve SLOs while optimizing for cost and throughput. It combines a design overview, scheduling rules, pragmatic implementation details, a profiling checklist, a benchmarking plan, and an on-call runbook for eviction-related incidents.

Goals
-----
- Preserve 99th percentile tail-latency SLOs for latency-sensitive routes.
- Maximize GPU utilization and reduce per-token cost using opportunistic consolidation.
- Provide deterministic, auditable behavior when eviction occurs (handoff + warm-up).
- Instrumentation and regression checks to detect adverse quality or latency impacts.

Scope
-----
This document applies to: 
- Multi-tenant inference runtime on heterogeneous GPU pools.
- Scheduler components that make per-request placement decisions and kernel handoff.
- Eviction/handoff logic used by the KVCache manager and session lifecycle controller.

Non-goals
---------
- Low-level kernel optimization details (covered separately in kernel-and-scheduling docs).
- Long-term capacity planning (covered in eng-sre/capacity-planning).

High-level design
-----------------
1. Priority Bands: requests are classified into 3 bands — latency-critical (band A), economical-high-throughput (band B), and best-effort/background (band C). Classification is a deterministically applied function using request metadata (route, customer tier, model variant, deadline hints).

2. Opportunistic Packing: when GPUs are underutilized, the scheduler will co-locate band B/C work with band A in non-blocking way using: 
   - kernel slice isolation (time-sliced or slot-based),
   - soft admission tokens (credit-based) and
   - KVCache partition isolation to avoid eviction storms.

3. Eviction Contracts: for every placement decision a compact, three-field eviction contract is recorded: 
   - keep_until (wall-clock or token-count),
   - restore_cost_budget (estimated extra tokens to rehydrate),
   - handoff_policy (none | live-migrate | graceful-evict-and-warmup).

4. Handoff & Warmup: for live-migrate or graceful-evict-and-warmup, the scheduler triggers an asynchronous warmup path: prefetch key KVCache prefixes, preload attention cache state where available, and bias routing for a short warming timeframe (configurable).

Design invariants (must hold)
----------------------------
- Deterministic fallback: when capacity shifts, the routing policy must produce consistent placement for identical inputs across a 60s window.
- Observability-first: every eviction must emit an EvictionEvent with unique id, contract fields, pre/post metrics.
- Cost-clarity: opportunistic packing must never increase the tail latency of Band A routes beyond configured SLO delta (default: +5ms).

Scheduler algorithms (summary)
----------------------------
- Primary: slot-based allocator with soft priorities. Each GPU exposes N time-slots per scheduling epoch. Band A gets preemptive access to earliest slots. Band B/C fill remaining slots opportunistically.
- Secondary: kernel affinity engine selects an execution kernel variant per-slot to maximize occupancy while respecting sequence length breakpoints.
- Preemption: cooperative preemption used for in-flight lower-priority requests; the runtime supports resumable slices for models that implement slice checkpoints.

Eviction contract lifecycle (sequence)
------------------------------------
1. Allocate -> scheduler writes eviction contract in placement store.
2. Emit EvictionEvent (state: planned).
3. If eviction requested, scheduler evaluates handoff_policy: 
   - live-migrate: initiate memory-transport protocol (only available for co-located shards and compatible kernels).
   - graceful-evict-and-warmup: drain active generation, spawn warmup worker on target GPU.
   - none: immediate eviction.
4. Emit EvictionEvent (state: executed) + post-metrics.
5. When restored, emit EvictionEvent (state: restored).

Configuration table (defaults and recommended ranges)
-----------------------------------------------------
| parameter | default | recommended range | notes |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|-------|
| scheduling.epoch_ms | 200 | 50-1000 | granularity of slot epochs; lower => finer preemption but more overhead |
| scheduling.slots_per_gpu | 8 | 4-32 | total logical slots to allocate |
| eviction.rehydrate_token_budget | 1200 | 200-10000 | estimated tokens allowed to restore a session; used to prioritize restoration |
| handoff.timeout_ms | 5000 | 1000-30000 | timeout for live-migrate attempts |
| packing.bandB_util_threshold | 0.45 | 0.2-0.9 | if GPU utilization < threshold, allow bandB opportunistic packing |

Sample eviction contract (YAML)
-------------------------------
```yaml
eviction_contract:
  id: "ev-20260210-abc123"
  keep_until: "2026-02-10T15:42:00Z"
  restore_cost_budget: "1500"
  handoff_policy: "graceful-evict-and-warmup"
  owner: "route:chat-stream-v2"
```

Placement CLI examples
----------------------
- Show current eviction contracts for a GPU node: 
  $ rtmctl node list-evictions --node gpu-34

- Force immediate eviction for contract id: 
  $ rtmctl eviction force --id ev-20260210-abc123 --reason "maintenance"

Observability and telemetry
--------------------------
Every eviction emits the following telemetry fields: 
- eviction_id, contract.keep_until, contract.rehydrate_budget, handoff_policy, pre_lat_p50/p95/p99, post_lat_p50/p95/p99, tokens_replayed, warmup_duration_ms, decision_reason.

Define alerts (recommended)
--------------------------
1. Eviction error rate > 0.5% over 1h for band A routes -> Pager (SEV2).
2. Warmup duration median > 1000ms for band A -> Pager (SEV3) + ticket.
3. Post-eviction tail-latency increase > 8ms sustained 15m -> Pager (SEV2).

Profiling and regression checklist
--------------------------------
Run the following when tuning packing or deploying new scheduler variants: 
1. Baseline profile capturing pre/post tail latency using production-shadow traces for 1h (use 10% traffic mirroring).
2. Instrument KVCache hit/miss per-session and tokens_replayed histogram.
3. Run synthetic microbursts (10x baseline QPS for 30s) and verify preemption does not increase 99th percentile beyond allowed delta.
4. Compare kernel occupancy and slot utilization heatmaps across nodes.

Benchmarking plan
-----------------
- Bench goal: show cost-per-1000-token reduction and 99th-latency impact for three workload shapes (short-chat, long-completion, embedding-batch).
- Bench matrix: vary packing.bandB_util_threshold across [0.25, 0.5, 0.75], epoch_ms across [100,200,500], and measure metrics for 4 hours.
- Success criteria: <= 5% increase in p99 for Band A, >= 10% utilization improvement, and per-token cost decrease >= 8% vs untuned baseline.

Runtime runbook: Eviction spike incident
---------------------------------------
1. Detection: alert fires when eviction error rate > configured threshold or post-eviction p99 delta > 8ms.
2. Initial triage (first 5 minutes): 
   - Check EvictionEvent stream for correlated ids and decision_reasons.
   - Identify node(s) with spike: rtmctl node tail-events --since 15m.
3. Immediate mitigation (if Band A affected): 
   - Disable opportunistic packing on affected pool: rtmctl config set packing.enabled=false --pool=pool-x
   - Increase scheduling.slots_per_gpu to reduce preemption frequency: rtmctl config set scheduling.slots_per_gpu=12 --pool=pool-x
4. If warmup failures observed: 
   - Check network transport logs for memory-transport errors.
   - Re-run warmup manually for top 5 sessions: rtmctl warmup replay --session <id> --target-node <node>
5. Post-incident: 
   - Run profiling checklist (see above).
   - Create postmortem with evacuation timeline, root cause, and follow-ups.

Rollout checklist for scheduler changes
-------------------------------------
1. Unit tests for slot allocation, eviction contract write/read, and fallthroughs.
2. Staging performance bench with shadow traffic (target: p99 within 3ms of baseline).
3. Gradual canary (5% traffic, 30m) with automated rollback if alerts trigger.
4. Increment to 25%, 50%, 100% with monitoring windows and manual check points.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Design + code owners: eng-serving-runtime/scheduler team (primary: Aisha Patel).
- Observability: eng-platform/dashboards (Evelyn Zhang).
- Incident escalation: eng-sre oncall.

Appendix A: Example observability query (pseudo-SQL)
--------------------------------------------------
SELECT eviction_id, handoff_policy, pre_p99, post_p99, (post_p99 - pre_p99) as delta
FROM eviction_events
WHERE route = 'chat-stream-v2' AND ts >= now() - interval '30m'
ORDER BY delta DESC

Appendix B: Implementation notes and gotchas
-------------------------------------------
- Keep contract writes idempotent: when reassigning, mutate in-place rather than append to avoid retention leaks.
- Coordinating live-migrate requires kernel compatibility matrix; explicit guards prevent attempts across incompatible kernels.
- Beware of eviction cascades: if bandB warmup floods nodes, fallback to immediate throttling for bandB for 60s.

Related reading
---------------
- See runtime-architecture docs on execution contracts and stable fallbacks for broader context.
- See quantization rollout safety playbook when eviction impacts quality due to model variant changes.
